title: The approved-artifact export reads the bundle's own training rows, pins the fit-time versions, binds every file, survives a storage failure and moves with a migrated workspace
request: The owner asked for a full review of another agent's commits, with authority to fix bugs; the reviewer confirmed seven findings on the approved-artifact service export (96e47f43).
spec: Fix the reviewer's confirmed findings on 96e47f43 with tests, editing only service.py, migrate.py, the final-approval binding lines of engine.py and their tests; add the missing test: approve run A, rerun final, export refused, re-approve, run B ships.
plan: read the capture, the binding and the migration
run the export, engine, workflow and migrate tests

decisions.decision: The training rows are read from the table as loaded (with a label file's join) through prepared.source_rows[bundle.train_idx], not from prepared.frame
decisions.why: source_rows are places in the table as loaded; prepared.frame lost the rows with no target or time and keeps the pre-sample order, so neither train_idx nor source_rows indexes it (the multiclass replica: 3,060 frame rows, 3,000 in X)

decisions.decision: A different host package version is said (checked.versions.differ, the check's how, the README), not refused
decisions.why: the image pins the versions the model was pickled with, which is right; refusing on any patch upgrade would make every approved model unexportable after a pip upgrade

decisions.decision: The capture writes all bytes to the local disk before storage is touched, and keeps every key and digest in the run record even when storage fails
decisions.why: the export can then finish the capture from those bytes, each checked against the digest the final run recorded: no refit, no second holdout read

decisions.decision: The approval binds every key, digest and the key reference (service.BIND_FIELDS, one list used by approve and export); a missing or incomplete binding is refused with 'approve the final stage again'
decisions.why: a binding of five fields left the parity rows, the monitoring plan and the key swappable; re-approving is cheap and reruns nothing

decisions.decision: Secrets move as files (0o700 folder, 0o600 files, never overwritten, never recorded in file storage); a differing target key is a difference
decisions.why: without the per-run key the migrated approved model cannot be exported; a key is never a stored record

change: dclab_rnd/studio/service.py (_training_frame, _package_versions, approval_binding, BIND_FIELDS, CHECK_ENV, local-first capture, recapture, version pins and python tag, minimal check env, shallow copy before strip), dclab_rnd/studio/engine.py (approve binds service.approval_binding), dclab_rnd/storage/migrate.py (artifacts/ and secrets/ copied and verified), tests/test_service_export.py, tests/test_storage_migrate_artifacts.py.

findings.defect: The serving record's training rows were other rows, holdout rows among them.
findings.scenario: fraud replica, quick (sampled, group split): 360 of 2,351 rows were training rows, 97 were holdout rows.
findings.cause: prepared.frame.iloc[bundle.train_idx]: train_idx indexes bundle.X, which a sample or a time split reorders; frame also lost rows.
findings.fix: load the table as prepare did and take source_rows[train_idx].
findings.test: tests/test_service_export.py test_the_serving_record_reads_the_bundle_s_own_training_rows (sampled and a time split that dropped rows)

findings.defect: requirements.txt pinned the exporting host's versions, not the ones the model was pickled with.
findings.scenario: a package upgraded between the final run and the export.
findings.fix: serving_meta.json keeps packages and python at capture; the export pins them, uses the Python minor in the Dockerfile and says when the host differs.

findings.defect: A migrated workspace lost every approved model's artifact and key.
findings.scenario: python -m dclab_rnd.storage migrate on a workspace with an approved final stage.
findings.cause: only data/ and exports/ were copied.
findings.fix: artifacts/ through file storage, secrets/ as owner-only files; verify reports a missing one.

findings.defect: A transient storage failure at capture made the approved model unexportable for good.
findings.scenario: the bucket times out during the final run's files.put.
findings.cause: bytes only in memory; the record kept no digests.
findings.fix: local bytes first, digests in the record, recoverable flag; export calls recapture, which checks each digest and stores again.
findings.test: ApprovalAndRecaptureTest (a changed local file refused, then recaptured with prepare, fit and load_table forbidden)

findings.defect: The approval did not bind the parity rows, monitoring plan or key reference.
findings.scenario: swap parity_fixture.json and its digest in the record after approval.
findings.fix: BIND_FIELDS bound and compared, legacy bindings refused until approved again.

findings.defect: The reload check's subprocess got the server's whole environment (API keys, database address, cloud credentials).
findings.scenario: any export on a configured server.

findings.defect: The capture deep-copied the whole training bundle only to drop it.
findings.fix: shallow copy, the spec-only stand-in, then deep copy.
findings.test: covered by the export parity tests

findings.defect: No test that a rerun of final needs a new approval before its model ships.
findings.fix: added. (see the change and its test)

measurements.name: Tests after the fixes: tests
measurements.result: {"what": "tests", "value": "test_service_export.py 20, test_engine_machines.py + test_workflow_run.py + test_storage_migrate.py 26, test_storage_migrate_artifacts.py 4: all pass", "verdict": "not scored"}

outcome: All seven findings fixed and the missing test added. Records approved under the five-field binding of 96e47f43 must be approved again before export.
lessons: Before indexing a frame with a split's positions, check which table those positions index: a sample, a dropped row or a time sort breaks the match silently.
Write bytes to the local disk and keep their digests before touching remote storage, so a failure can be finished without redoing the work.
Give a check subprocess only the environment it needs.
risks: Capture now reads the table a second time at the final run (the cost of one load).
A host whose packages differ from the fit-time ones still exports; the check ran on the host's packages, which the README and checked.versions say.
